page.layout: One page of running text in one column. Marginal notes in the left margin, beside the lines they belong to: "Toxica.", "morfus rabidi.", "hydro- phobia.", "Dolor dentium.", "Lienosi." Running head and page number at the top. Catchword "cibo" at the right below the last line.

main_text.p: Toxica.Vomitiones quoque homini canis monstrasse videtur, aliosque ex eo maire[?] lau-datos vsus,hic referre operæ pretium erit, quia hoc animali nullum fere familiarius homini. In canis rabidi morsu tuetur ab morsus rabidi.hydrophobia seu pauore aquæ,capitis canini cinis illitus vulneri. Oportet autem,inquit Plinius l.29.c.5.hydro- phobia.omnia comburi in vase fictili nouo argilla circumlito atque in furnum indito. Idem & in potione proficit. Quidam obid edendum dederunt: alii vermem è ca-dauere canino adalligauere, menstruauein panno subdidere calici,aut intus ipsius cau-dæ pilos combustos infuêre[?] vulneri. Cor ca-ninum habentes fugiunt canes. Non latrant vero linguâ canina in calceamento subdita pollici. Iecur caninum vtilissime in rabie morsis datur, si possit fieri,crudum manden-dum, si minus, quoque modo coctum, aut jus coctis carnibus. Saliuntur & carnes eo-rum qui rabidi fuerunt ad eadem remedia in cibo dandæ. Quin & catuli statim necan-tur in aqua, ad sexum ejus qui momorderit, Dolor dentium.vt iecur crudum ex iis deuoretur. Caninus dens finister maximus, circumscarificato eo, qui doleat, dolorem tollit. Idem præstat collutio caninis dentibus decoctis in vino ad dimidias,nec non cinis eorum, qui rabie perierunt, capitum crematorum fine carni-bus. Lienosi.Lien caninus viuenti exemtus inque cibo

page.notes: Printed page number 431 at the head, read as "431". Running head "De Vita" in small capitals. Catchword "cibo" at the lower right. Text ends mid-sentence ("inque") and continues on the next page. Doubtful readings: "maire" (possibly maiore), "infuêre" (the accent on e is unclear). "obid" is printed as one word, left as printed. "menstruauein" left as printed. Marginal labels: "Dolor" and "dentium." are printed as two lines of one label; given as one note. Italic labels marked with <i>. Printed "jus" in "jus coctis" written as "jus", consonant j. "vsus" and "fictili" with long s printed as plain s.
